title: enhancement: add Renovate bot trust chain and dependency impact assessment (parity with Dependabot)
body:
## Description

Pulse has a mature trust chain for Dependabot PRs (`_is_trusted_dependabot_update_pr()` in `pulse-merge-gates.sh`) that verifies bot identity, same-repo branches, commit authorship, dependency-file-only diffs, an allowlist, and security scans — then auto-approves and auto-merges trusted updates.

Renovate (`renovate[bot]`) has no equivalent handling. This causes two observable problems:

1. **Renovate PRs permanently stuck**: pulse-merge skips all Renovate PRs with "author renovate[bot] is not a collaborator", leaving them open indefinitely with no review or merge path.

2. **Dependency Dashboard dispatch noise**: Renovate's meta-tracking "Dependency Dashboard" issues (one per repo) are picked up by `dispatch_with_dedup` every cycle, fail classification, and inflate the `unclassified_signal` counter. In a 16-repo org this generates ~90 false dispatch failures per 24h from just 3 Dashboard issues.

## Expected Behavior

### Part A — Renovate trust chain (parity with Dependabot)

A new `_is_trusted_renovate_update_pr()` function in `pulse-merge-gates.sh`, mirroring the Dependabot trust chain:

- Author = `renovate[bot]` / `app/renovate`
- Branch = `renovate/*` in same-repo (not a fork)
- All commits authored by `renovate[bot]`
- Diff touches only dependency files (requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, Dockerfile, docker-compose, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, composer.json/lock, go.mod/sum, Cargo.toml/lock, etc.)
- No terminal security-scan failures
- Dependency on maintainer allowlist (`trusted-renovate-updates.conf`, same format as `trusted-dependabot-updates.conf`)

For allowlisted dependencies with passing CI: auto-approve + auto-merge, identical to Dependabot path.

### Part B — Dependency impact assessment comment

For Renovate PRs that pass trust verification but are NOT on the auto-merge allowlist, pulse could post a one-time structured impact comment extracted from the Renovate PR body (which always contains structured metadata):

- Package name, old → new version, semver bump type (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH)
- CI status summary
- Merge confidence (from Renovate's Mend.io badges)
- Brief changelog highlights

Decision matrix:

| Semver | CI | Allowlisted | Action |
|--------|-----|-------------|--------|
| PATCH | green | yes | Auto-merge |
| PATCH | green | no | Impact comment, defer to reviewer |
| MINOR | green | yes | Auto-approve, merge after cooldown |
| MINOR | green | no | Impact comment, defer to reviewer |
| MAJOR | any | any | Never auto-merge, impact comment with changelog |
| any | red | any | Impact comment with failed CI info, skip merge |

This gives reviewers actionable context instead of a naked PR sitting in the queue.

### Part C — Dependency Dashboard early-skip

Add title-match `"Dependency Dashboard"` (or author=`renovate[bot]` + label=`dependencies`) to the early-skip block in `dispatch_with_dedup` (alongside `consolidated`, `parent-task`, etc.). These are Renovate meta-tracking issues, not implementable work items.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Renovate configured on a repo managed by pulse
2. Renovate creates PRs (e.g., `chore(deps): update dependency X to vN`)
3. Observe pulse-merge.log: "author renovate[bot] is not a collaborator" — PR skipped
4. Renovate creates "Dependency Dashboard" issue
5. Observe pulse.log: repeated `unclassified_signal` failures every dispatch cycle

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.20.85
- **Latest version**: 3.20.85
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

- The existing `_is_trusted_dependabot_update_pr()` (lines ~131-187 of `pulse-merge-gates.sh`) and `trusted-dependabot-updates.conf` provide the exact pattern to follow.
- Renovate PR bodies always contain a structured table with package, version change, age, and confidence — making automated parsing straightforward.
- Part C (Dashboard skip) is a ~5 LOC fix that eliminates ~90 false failures/day immediately.

title: pulse blockedBy fail-closed policy blocks dependency-free dispatch during GraphQL exhaustion
body:
## Problem
PR #24584 intentionally preserved fail-closed behavior when native GitHub `blockedBy` lookup is unavailable and the issue body has no fallback `blocked-by` markers. In practice, during GraphQL exhaustion this blocks large portions of dispatch even for issues that do not declare dependencies.

This is safer than the original GH#24576 behavior, but too broad operationally: a transient native lookup failure becomes a queue-wide dispatch stop.

## Evidence
Recent pulse log pattern:

```text
is_blocked_by_unresolved: #N native blockedBy lookup unavailable — checking body fallback (GH#24576)
is_blocked_by_unresolved: #N native blockedBy lookup unavailable and no body blocked-by markers found — skipping dispatch (GH#24576)
Dispatch blocked for #N in <repo>: unresolved blocked-by dependency (t1927)
Dispatch_max: #N (<repo>) pre-launch failure reason=unclassified_signal
```

Counts from one current pulse log:

- `native blockedBy lookup unavailable`: 317
- `native blockedBy lookup unavailable and no body blocked-by markers found`: 316
- `Dispatch blocked ... unresolved blocked-by dependency`: 316
- `pre-launch failure reason=unclassified_signal`: 444
- `GraphQL budget EXHAUSTED`: 533

Relevant code:

- `pulse-dep-graph.sh:623-653`: `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships()` returns `3` when the GraphQL native relationship lookup is unavailable.
- `pulse-dep-graph.sh:917-924`: `is_blocked_by_unresolved()` distinguishes native rc `3` from confirmed blocked/clear.
- `pulse-dep-graph.sh:941-947`: when no body `blocked-by` markers exist and native rc is `3`, the function returns `0` (blocked), causing dispatch to skip.
- `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1642-1658`: `_dlw_blocked_by_hard_stop()` treats return `0` as hard-stop before worker bootstrap.

## Why this matters
This preserves UI-only native blocker safety, but under GraphQL exhaustion it misclassifies every issue whose native relationship lookup cannot be checked and whose body has no markers. The dispatch queue spends cycles rechecking and blocking candidates instead of dispatching safe work or using available cached state.

## Suggested fix
Keep fail-closed for genuinely unknown dependency state, but narrow it with available evidence:

1. If native lookup returns `3`, consult the dependency graph cache before failing closed.
2. If the cache is fresh enough and contains no `blocked_by` entry for the issue, allow dispatch when body has no markers.
3. If cache is missing/stale/unavailable, preserve current fail-closed behavior for UI-only native blocker safety.
4. Emit a distinct low-cardinality reason such as `blocked_by_native_lookup_unavailable` instead of `unclassified_signal` so pulse stats separate this policy gate from true unknowns.

Alternative: add a REST-backed issue relationship probe if GitHub exposes equivalent data without GraphQL cost; otherwise cache-gated fail-open is the lower-cost path.

## Verification
- Add a shell test for `is_blocked_by_unresolved()` where:
  - `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` returns `3`.
  - issue body has no `blocked-by` markers.
  - dep-graph cache is fresh and has no `blocked_by` entry for the issue.
  - Expected: return `1` (safe to dispatch).
- Add a complementary test where cache is missing/stale and native rc `3`; expected: return `0` (current fail-closed behavior).
- Add/adjust dispatch classification test so this path is not counted as `unclassified_signal`.
- Run the relevant shell tests plus ShellCheck on changed scripts.

Refs: #24576, PR #24584, #24604.

title: tbd: bug: normalize issue and PR status after worker_complete linked PR
body:
## Problem

An auto-dispatched issue can remain labelled `status:available` after a worker completes and opens a linked PR. The linked PR can also keep or receive `status:available`, leaving issue/PR lifecycle state inconsistent with the actual review state.

## Evidence

Observed on AwardsApp issue #6616 and PR #6642:

- Issue #6616 had `auto-dispatch` and was picked up by pulse/dispatch.
- First worker released with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_branch_orphan`.
- Second worker released with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete`.
- PR #6642 was opened with `Resolves #6616`.
- `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh status 6616 awardsapp/awardsapp` returned no active dispatch.
- Before manual normalization, issue #6616 still had `status:available` despite the linked open PR.
- Before manual normalization, PR #6642 also had `status:available`.
- Manual normalization changed #6616 and #6642 to `status:in-review` and removed stale `status:available`.

Relevant local code evidence:

- `shared-constants.sh::clear_active_status_on_release` preserves `status:in-review` when a linked PR exists, but does not actively add `status:in-review` or remove stale `status:available` in the linked-PR branch.
- The same helper only adds `status:available` when no linked PR exists.
- `full-loop-helper-commit.sh::_label_issue_in_review` does set the linked issue to `in-review`, but the observed path suggests worker/PR lifecycle can bypass or race that normalization.

## Expected behaviour

When a worker completes and an open linked PR exists for the issue:

1. The issue should have `status:in-review`.
2. The issue should not have `status:available`, `status:queued`, `status:claimed`, or `status:in-progress`.
3. The linked PR should have `status:in-review`.
4. The linked PR should not have `status:available`.
5. The release/cleanup path should be idempotent and race-safe with PR merge cleanup.

## Suggested implementation area

Start with:

- `scripts/shared-constants.sh` — `clear_active_status_on_release`
- `scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` — `_label_issue_in_review`
- worker completion / PR creation paths that emit `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete`
- any PR label normalization helper used by pulse/full-loop

Likely fix: in the linked-open-PR branch, explicitly remove `status:available` and ensure `status:in-review` on the issue. Also normalize the linked PR label to remove `status:available` and add `status:in-review` where safe.

## Verification

Add or update tests/fixtures around claim release with a linked open PR:

- auto-dispatch issue starts with `status:available`
- worker creates PR body containing `Resolves #<issue>`
- release reason is `worker_complete`
- final issue labels include `status:in-review` and exclude `status:available`
- final PR labels include `status:in-review` and exclude `status:available`
- merged/done race remains protected: a late release must not regress `status:done`

title: Worker startup stalls do not fail over to alternate provider after initial model no-activity
body:
## Description

Worker dispatch can select an initial provider/model via `--initial-model`, but a startup no-activity stall (`watchdog_startup_continue` / `startup_no_model_activity`) does not appear to trigger alternate-provider failover.

Observed recent worker metrics showed repeated startup stalls on one provider/model while another provider was available and succeeding on other workers. The retry path stayed on the original provider/model for the affected tasks instead of switching to an alternate provider.

Private repo names, local paths, and issue identifiers are intentionally omitted.

## Expected Behavior

When a worker starts, produces startup output, but no model activity before the watchdog timeout, the bounded continuation path should either:

1. switch to an alternate provider/model after the configured continuation budget is exhausted, or
2. set a failure reason handled by `_cmd_run_prepare_retry` so the existing retry/failover path rotates providers.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 24h
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh providers --since 24h
```

**Actual output**:

Sanitized summary from the observing session:

```text
Result class: watchdog_startup_continue
Launch failure cause: startup_no_model_activity
Kill reason: no_output_stall
Next action: retry_fresh_or_inspect_local_runtime
Provider/model: openai/openai/gpt-5.4
Count: 12 startup no-activity continuations in the sampled window

Provider/model usage in same window:
openai/openai/gpt-5.4: success=35, other_failure=32
anthropic/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6: success=12, other_failure=6
```

The same affected worker sessions showed repeated startup stalls on the original provider/model. No per-task evidence showed automatic retry on the alternate provider.

**Expected output**:

After startup no-activity continuation is exhausted, logs should show a provider/model switch similar to the rate-limit path:

```text
<provider> startup_no_model_activity detected; retrying with alternate provider model <next_model>
```

**Causal code**:

`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` correctly passes dispatcher-selected models as initial preferences rather than hard pins:

```bash
.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1367-1371
```

`headless-runtime-helper.sh` classifies startup output without model activity as `watchdog_startup_continue` and returns `78`:

```bash
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:827-831
```

The `78` path eventually falls through to `_cmd_run_prepare_retry` after continuation budget is exhausted:

```bash
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1881-1928
```

But `_cmd_run_prepare_retry` only switches provider for `auth_error` or `rate_limit`:

```bash
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1123-1147
```

Therefore `watchdog_startup_continue` / `startup_no_model_activity` is documented as “falling through to provider rotation” but does not satisfy the retry function’s switch condition.

**Call-site sweep**:

```text
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1109 _cmd_run_prepare_retry()
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1134 only auth_error/rate_limit switch
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:828 _run_result_label="watchdog_startup_continue"
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1072 startup_no_model_activity evidence mapping
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1922 comment says fall through to provider rotation
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1926 calls _cmd_run_prepare_retry
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a worker with an initial model selected by pulse.
2. Cause the worker process to emit startup/runtime setup output but no model activity until the watchdog timeout.
3. Let `HEADLESS_WATCHDOG_CONTINUE_MAX_RETRIES` exhaust.
4. Observe that `_cmd_run_prepare_retry` does not switch provider because `_run_failure_reason` is not `auth_error` or `rate_limit`.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually inspected worker metrics to identify `startup_no_model_activity`.
- Manually inspected provider usage to confirm another provider was available.
- Manually traced the shell retry path across:
  - `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
  - `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
  - `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`

No runtime workaround was applied.

## Environment

Sanitized diagnostics:

```text
aidevops version: 3.20.85
Latest version: 3.20.85
AI Assistant: OpenCode
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
Shell: bash 5.2.21
gh CLI: 2.89.0
```

Local install paths and private working context omitted for privacy.

## Additional Context

Duplicate checks performed:

```text
gh issue list -R marcusquinn/aidevops --state all --search "startup_no_model_activity failover provider rotation watchdog_startup_continue" --limit 10
=> []

gh pr list -R marcusquinn/aidevops --state merged --search "startup_no_model_activity failover provider rotation" --limit 5
=> no output

gh pr list -R marcusquinn/aidevops --state open --search "startup_no_model_activity failover provider rotation" --limit 5
=> no output
```

Recent commits touching suspect files in the last week:

```text
09cf9fd15 auto-recover: orphaned worker branch for #24796 (#24811)
f312d7e88 GH#24798: fix: harden orphan recovery base handling (#24804)
1d96ad87b fix: use configured base for orphan recovery (#24799)
6777ee4d8 fix: isolate pulse worker logs per user (#24622)
```

Suggested fix direction:

- Treat `watchdog_startup_continue` / `startup_no_model_activity` as eligible for alternate-provider retry after bounded continuation is exhausted, or
- set `_run_failure_reason="startup_no_model_activity"` and teach `_cmd_run_prepare_retry` to switch providers for that reason.

title: Fix task-counter reconciliation race handling
body:
## Task

Fix claim-task-id pre-reconciliation so retryable task-counter reconciliation races do not abort issue creation before allocation.

## Context

title: tbd: bug: respect develop dispatch base in single-issue worker helper
body:
## Problem

`dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch` creates worker branches from `origin/<default-branch>` by resolving `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`. In repos that intentionally use a `develop` PR target while GitHub/default branch remains `main`, manual dispatch creates worktrees from the wrong base.

Observed in AwardsApp:

- Repository workflow requires feature branches and PRs to target `develop`.
- `origin/HEAD` points at `main`.
- `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch 6639 awardsapp/awardsapp` created `feature/auto-20260617-000933-gh6639` tracking `origin/main`.
- That branch was based on old `main` commit `7a3d05b484`, not current `develop`.
- The worker had to be stopped before it produced a stale/main-based PR.

## Secondary failure observed

Trying to compensate manually with `worktree-helper.sh add --base origin/develop` created a correct worktree, but `headless-runtime-helper.sh` then refused it with:

```text
[fatal] worker worktree already has a live owner
```

The owner was the interactive OpenCode process, because the helper registered the worktree to the current session. A direct `git worktree add -b ... origin/develop` avoided registry ownership and allowed the headless worker to claim the worktree successfully.

## Expected behaviour

Manual single-issue dispatch should respect repo-specific integration branch policy, not blindly use `origin/HEAD`.

For repos with a develop-flow configuration, dispatch should create branches from `origin/develop` and PRs should target `develop`.

## Suggested implementation area

Start with:

- `scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
  - `_dsi_default_branch`
  - `_dsi_create_worktree`
- `scripts/worktree-helper.sh` ownership registration when `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_AUTO_CLAIM=1`
- repo config sources such as `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` or a per-repo branch-policy config, if one exists

Possible fixes:

1. Add an explicit `--base REF` option to `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch`, passing through to `worktree-helper.sh add --base REF`.
2. Honor `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE` / `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_BASE_REF` in `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`.
3. Add repo-configured dispatch base branch support, with fallback to `origin/HEAD` only when no policy exists.
4. Ensure the helper-created worktree can be transferred to headless runtime without `worker_worktree_live_owner` when it is intentionally pre-created for dispatch.

## Verification

Add/extend tests around manual dispatch worktree creation:

- repo default branch is `main`
- repo dispatch/PR target is `develop`
- manual dispatch creates a worktree from `origin/develop`, not `origin/main`
- worker can claim the pre-created worktree without `worker_worktree_live_owner`
- fallback still uses `origin/HEAD` for repos with no configured dispatch base

title: gh_pr_list called ~240+ times per pulse cycle — 46/48 call sites bypass existing pulse_pr_list_get cache
body:
## Description

`gh_pr_list` is called ~240+ times per single pulse cycle. Twelve or more independent
stages each call `gh_pr_list` for the same repos in the same cycle, with no cache sharing
between them. The existing `pulse_pr_list_get` cache (TTL=3600s) is designed for exactly
this purpose, but only 2 of ~48 call sites use it.

Each call costs ~0.5-0.8s of API latency. At 240 calls/cycle, that's 2-3 minutes of
wall-clock time spent just on redundant PR listings — not including the secondary calls
(`gh_pr_view`, checks, etc.) that follow each list.

When the GitHub API budget is tight, redundant calls accelerate rate-limit exhaustion,
triggering secondary cooldown, REST fallbacks, and cascading slowdowns across the
entire pulse cycle.

## Expected Behavior

Stages within the same pulse cycle should share PR list data via `pulse_pr_list_get`
instead of each calling `gh_pr_list` independently. A single `--state open` list per
repo per cycle should suffice; cached results (TTL=3600s) should be reused by dispatch,
merge pass, dirty sweep, capacity alloc, quality debt, and other consumers.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
# Count how many times gh_pr_list is called in a single pulse cycle
grep "gh_pr_list\|pulse_pr_list_get" .agents/scripts/ --include="*.sh" -r \
  -g '!*test*' -g '!*.bak' | grep -v "function\|_snapshot\|record_call"
```

**Actual output**:

48 references to `gh_pr_list` across the codebase. Only 2 of those use
`pulse_pr_list_get` (the cache wrapper). The remaining 46 call raw `gh_pr_list`.

**Cache users (2 call sites):**
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-queue-governor.sh:58` — `pulse_pr_list_get`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:375` — `pulse_pr_list_get`

**Raw `gh_pr_list` callers (46+ sites, representative sample):**
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:73` — delta PR list
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:233` — full PR list
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:288` — daily cap
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-infra.sh:243` — infra PR list
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-infra.sh:336` — changed PR list
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:609` — dispatch PR count
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:248` — dispatch core
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:293` — dispatch core
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:422` — merge pass PR list
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:847` — merge pass children
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh:141` — capacity check
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh:427` — capacity alloc
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:1023` — dirty sweep
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-quality-debt.sh:91` — quality debt
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh:116` — ancillary dispatch
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh:65` — dedup
- (and ~28 more across claim lifecycle, worktree cleanup, reconcile, triage, etc.)

**Expected output**:

At most ~16 calls per cycle (one per pulse-enabled repo), served from
`pulse_pr_list_get` cache across all stages.

**Causal code**:

The `pulse_pr_list_get` cache wrapper already exists:
`.agents/scripts/pulse-pr-list-cache.sh:115` — TTL=3600s, per-cycle cache
`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:146` — snapshot cache (TTL=15s)

But most callers never route through it. The `gh_pr_list` function (line 444 of
`shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh`) has no visibility into which stage is calling it,
so it cannot enforce cross-stage sharing.

**Call-site sweep**:

See the full list above. Key observation: within a single cycle, the same repo's
`--state open` PR list is fetched by prefetch (3x), dispatch (2x), merge pass,
capacity alloc (2x), dirty sweep, quality debt, and ancillary dispatch — 11+
independent fetches for the same data.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy pulse on a set of 10+ repos with active PRs.
2. Observe API call telemetry during a pulse cycle.
3. Count `gh_pr_list` invocations per repo per cycle.
4. Compare against the expected 1 (cached) result.

## Workarounds Applied

None — this was discovered during a pulse-cycle performance analysis.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.20.86
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.89.0

## Additional Context

The duplicate calls compound with two other performance patterns:
1. Each `gh_pr_list` call with different `--json` flags creates a different cache key,
   so even when the 15s snapshot cache is enabled, callers requesting different fields
   miss each other's cache entries.
2. Under rate-limit pressure, each raw call either consumes GraphQL budget or triggers
   REST fallback — both have a cost even when the result would be identical to a
   call made 2 seconds earlier by a different stage.

title: Pulse REST fallback death spiral — secondary cooldown too short, dispatch-dedup parallel amplification, no REST budget check
body:
## Description

When the GraphQL API budget is exhausted, pulse falls back to REST API calls. During this fallback, the REST core rate limit (5000/h) is also quickly exhausted, producing HTTP 403 responses. The system then enters a death spiral:

1. GraphQL budget exhausted → pulse switches to REST fallback
2. REST core budget also exhausted → dispatch-dedup-helper.sh and other components get HTTP 403
3. Secondary cooldown only blocks retries for ~250 seconds, but API reset takes 30-60 minutes
4. After cooldown expires, pulse retries and immediately hits 403 again
5. Multiple parallel processes (dispatch-dedup-helper.sh) retry the same issue simultaneously, burning REST budget faster
6. Health heartbeat never updates because the health subsystem cannot get API responses
7. Scheduler continues cycling, consuming API budget on futile retries

### Observed metrics (last 24h)

- `dispatch_candidate_failed: 1700`
- `dispatch_worker_spawned: 21` (only 21 workers for 1700 candidates)
- `pulse_dispatch_rest_fallback: 999`
- `pulse_graphql_budget_reserve_mode: 24`
- `pulse_graphql_budget_stage_deferred: 150`
- `dispatch_candidate_failed_reason_launch_error: 167`
- `dispatch_candidate_failed_reason_policy_gate: 746`
- `dispatch_candidate_failed_reason_unclassified_signal: 678`
- `dispatch_worker_launch_failed: 13`
- `pulse_events_tickle_stale: 53` vs `pulse_events_tickle_fresh: 3`
- `pulse_merge_stuck_escalations_filed: 5`
- Health heartbeat stale: 267 minutes

### Runner health

`runner-health.json` shows `consecutive_zero_attempts: 1`, all 20 most recent outcomes have `signal: "no_worker_process"`. The circuit breaker hasn't been updated since June 12.

## Expected Behavior

The system should handle API budget exhaustion gracefully:

1. When both GraphQL and REST budgets are depleted, pulse should pause (not retry) until the API reset window
2. Parallel retries for the same issue should be deduplicated at the retry layer
3. Health heartbeat should include API budget state and signal "degraded"
4. Secondary cooldown duration should match the API reset window, not a fixed 250 seconds

## Bugs Identified

### Bug 1: REST secondary cooldown too short (~250s vs 30-60 min API reset window)

The secondary cooldown mechanism (`expires_at` in `gh-secondary-cooldown.json`) only blocks retries for ~250 seconds. The GitHub API core rate limit resets on a rolling 60-minute window. After 250 seconds, pulse retries REST calls and immediately hits 403 again, because the REST budget hasn't been restored.

### Bug 2: dispatch-dedup-helper.sh has no REST budget awareness

When GraphQL is exhausted and pulse falls back to REST, dispatch-dedup-helper.sh uses `gh api` (REST) to check issue assignee state. There's no pre-flight check of `x-ratelimit-remaining` or REST core budget before making these calls. Each call that gets a 403 wastes a REST budget slot.

### Bug 3: Parallel retry amplification

Multiple instances of dispatch-dedup-helper.sh are spawned simultaneously for the same issue (observed: 6+ processes for Majowka/mesh-manager#66), all hitting REST endpoints and all getting 403. This multiplies REST budget consumption by the concurrency factor.

### Bug 4: Health heartbeat decoupled from API budget state

The pulse health heartbeat (267 min stale) does not factor in API rate limit state. If both GraphQL and REST budgets are depleted, the heartbeat should report "degraded" and the scheduler should defer cycles until budget is restored.

### Bug 5: dispatch-dedup-helper.sh error response amplification

When dispatch-dedup-helper.sh receives a 403 from GitHub, it does not check for rate-limit in the HTTP response before retrying. The 403 error body containing `{"message":"API rate limit exceeded..."}` is passed through to subsequent processing without triggering a circuit break.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
# Observe pulse dispatch failing with 403 during REST fallback:
ps aux | grep dispatch-dedup
```

**Actual output**:

```
dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned 66 Majowka/mesh-manager {"message":"API rate limit exceeded for user ID 273984258...", "status": "403"}
dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned 66 Majowka/mesh-manager {"message":"API rate limit exceeded...", "status": "403"}
dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned 66 Majowka/mesh-manager {"message":"API rate limit exceeded...", "status": "403"}
```

(6+ parallel processes, all with the same 403)

**Expected output**:

After first 403, the system should stop retrying the same issue and wait for budget restoration.

**Call-site sweep**:

```bash
rg "gh api" .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh
rg "gh-secondary-cooldown\|secondary.cooldown\|cooldown_expires" .agents/scripts/
rg "REST.*budget\|rest.*remaining\|ratelimit_remaining" .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh
```

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.20.86
- **Latest version**: 3.20.86
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-17)

## Additional Context

Relevant recent fixes:
- #24952 — harden pulse GitHub reliability (merged today, fixes gh shim bypass and merge routine budget)
- #24946 — blockedBy fail-closed policy (open, partially related)
- #23605 — enforce shared GitHub secondary-rate-limit cooldown across pulse and stats (closed)
- #24855 — evaluation: pulse GitHub API pacing after boot and cooldown (closed)
- #24547 — pulse ignores GitHub API rate-limit response headers (closed)

title: pulse-merge-routine: in-cycle merge bypasses lock — 60s guard too short for 600s timeout, causing 2-4 parallel instances
body:
## Description

`pulse-merge-routine.sh` has two separate launch paths, but only one of them checks the file-based lock, causing multiple simultaneous merge routine instances.

### Two launch paths

| Path | Trigger | Lock check |
|---|---|---|
| **In-cycle** | `pulse-wrapper.sh` → `merge_ready_prs_all_repos()` | ❌ **None** — called directly, bypasses `_pmr_acquire_lock()` |
| **Standalone** | cron/launchd → `pulse-merge-routine.sh run` | ✅ `_pmr_acquire_lock()` via `cmd_run()` |

### The duplication cycle

```
t=0    : standalone starts → acquires lock → merge work begins
t=60   : pulse-wrapper guard expires (timestamp file > 60s old)
t=60s+ : pulse-wrapper calls merge_ready_prs_all_repos() — no lock check → 2nd instance
t=120  : cron spawns new standalone → lock held → exit 0 ✅
t=300  : in-cycle merge still running (timeout 600s)
t=600  : standalone times out → releases lock
t=601  : new standalone → acquires lock
t=660  : guard expires again → another in-cycle merge
```

**Result**: 2-4 simultaneous merge routine instances observed consistently.

### Evidence

Observed in production (2026-06-17 11:10 UTC):

```
PID       TIME  CMD
3382014  10:02  bash pulse-merge-routine.sh run   (about to timeout)
3382644  10:01  bash pulse-merge-routine.sh run   (about to timeout)
3515599  01:56  bash pulse-merge-routine.sh run   (lock owner)
3516442  01:55  bash pulse-merge-routine.sh run   (new, bypassed lock)
3516892  01:30  bash pulse-merge-routine.sh run   (new, bypassed lock)
3516913  01:29  bash pulse-merge-routine.sh run   (new, bypassed lock)
```

Lock file at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/locks/pulse-merge-routine.lock/pid` contains PID 3519936, but 5 other instances are running simultaneously.

### Consequences

1. **API budget waste**: each merge routine consumes 100+ REST/GraphQL calls. 4 parallel instances burn 4x the budget.
2. **Rate limit exhaustion accelerates**: the parallel instances consume the hourly API budget in 15-20 minutes instead of 60 minutes.
3. **Dispatch starvation**: merge routines consume API budget that should be used for dispatching workers, causing `no_worker_process` and dispatch failure cascades.
4. **Noise in logs and metrics**: duplicate merge routines report overlapping successes and failures, making monitoring unreliable.

## Expected Behavior

Only one merge routine instance should run at any given time, regardless of launch path.

## Root Cause

### Bug 1: `merge_ready_prs_all_repos()` does not check the lock

**File:** `pulse-wrapper.sh:1211-1212`

```bash
run_stage_with_timeout "deterministic_merge_pass" "$PRE_RUN_STAGE_TIMEOUT" \
    merge_ready_prs_all_repos || true
```

The in-cycle path calls `merge_ready_prs_all_repos` directly without calling `_pmr_acquire_lock()` first.

**Fix:** either:
- Check the lock before calling `merge_ready_prs_all_repos`, or
- Have `merge_ready_prs_all_repos` call `_pmr_acquire_lock()` internally

### Bug 2: 60-second guard is too short for a 600s timeout

**File:** `pulse-wrapper.sh:1192-1213`

The guard at `pulse-wrapper.sh:1205` skips the in-cycle merge pass only if the standalone routine ran within the last **60 seconds**. But the merge routine timeout is **600 seconds** (the `PULSE_MERGE_ROUTINE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` default). The guard expires 60x faster than the merge routine completes.

**Fix:** the guard should either:
- Match the timeout value, not 60s, or
- Check if a merge routine is actually still running (via lock/PID file) rather than relying on timestamp

### Bug 3: No PID-file check in the guard

The guard at line 1196-1208 only reads a timestamp file (`pulse-merge-routine-last-run`). It never checks if the lock directory exists or if the lock-owner PID is still alive. A PID/lock check would accurately detect a running instance regardless of elapsed time.

## Suggested Fix

In `pulse-wrapper.sh`, replace the timestamp-only guard at lines 1196-1208 with a combined check:

```bash
# Check lock first — if lock owner is alive, skip regardless of elapsed time
if [[ -d "$LOCK_DIR" ]] && [[ -f "${LOCK_DIR}/pid" ]]; then
    local lock_pid
    lock_pid=$(cat "${LOCK_DIR}/pid" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    if [[ "$lock_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$lock_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "[pulse-wrapper] deterministic_merge_pass: skipping (merge routine pid=${lock_pid} still running)" >>"$LOGFILE"
        _pmr_skip=1
    fi
fi

# Fall back to timestamp guard only if no lock is held
if [[ "$_pmr_skip" -eq 0 ]] && [[ -f "$_pulse_merge_routine_last_run" ]]; then
    ... existing timestamp check ...
fi
```

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.20.86
- **Latest version**: 3.20.86
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## See Also

- #24904 — merge routine ignores GraphQL budget env vars (related timeout cascade)
- #24961 — pulse REST fallback death spiral (merge duplication compounds API budget exhaustion)
- #21247 — split merge pass into dedicated 60s plist (prior work, did not address lock bypass)

## Description

### Evidence

```
PID 3846937 (1h13min) ← LOCK OWNER
 └─ 3890020 (10min)
    └─ 3918997 (8min)
       ├─ 4116780 (14s)
       │  └─ 4118335 + 4124391
       ├─ 4116993 (14s)
       │  └─ 4118883 + 4124160
       ├─ 4117222 (13s)
       │  └─ 4119374 + 4124097
       └─ 4123906 (1s)
          └─ 4124352 + 4124363
```

14 concurrent `pulse-wrapper.sh` processes, forming a parent-child-grandchild chain. The lock at `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.lockdir/pid` contains the root PID (3846937) — but 13 other instances are also running.

The same recursive pattern was observed for `pulse-merge-routine.sh` (see #24962), where 6 instances ran simultaneously despite a lock.

### Expected Behavior

Only one `pulse-wrapper.sh` instance should run at any time. If the lock is held by a living PID, new instances must exit before doing any work.

### Root Cause Analysis

The instance lock in `pulse-instance-lock.sh:264` uses `mkdir` atomicity:

```bash
acquire_instance_lock() {
    if ! mkdir "$LOCKDIR" 2>/dev/null; then
        _handle_existing_lock || return 1
    fi
```

If `mkdir` fails, `_handle_existing_lock` checks if the lock owner PID is alive. If alive, it returns 1 (exit).

However, the recursive spawning defeats this because:

1. The parent wrapper (3846937) holds the lock for 1h+
2. At some point, the parent's code path spawns a child wrapper
3. The child wrapper either:
   - Acquires the lock BEFORE the parent's lock is fully established (race window)
   - Or inherits the lock through FD inheritance (despite mkdir being FD-free, the stale-reclaim logic in `_handle_existing_lock` may reclaim the lock from a living parent under certain conditions)
   - Or the parent temporarily releases the lock (e.g., during pre-LLM drop), the child acquires it, then the parent re-acquires it

### Consequences

1. **API budget waste**: 14 wrappers simultaneously making API calls burn the rate limit 14x faster
2. **Dispatch starvation**: most API budget consumed by duplicate wrapper overhead, leaving no capacity for actual worker dispatch
3. **Log noise**: duplicate wrappers write overlapping log entries, making monitoring unreliable
4. **Self-reinforcing spiral**: more wrappers = more API calls = more rate limiting = more timeouts = more stale-lock triggers = more wrapper spawns

### Suggested Fix

The `acquire_instance_lock` mechanism needs an additional safety layer:

1. **PGREP guard**: Before acquiring the lock, check if ANY other `pulse-wrapper.sh` process is running with the same PID namespace. If found, exit immediately without trying to reclaim.

2. **Nested-spawn detection**: Track spawning depth. If `pulse-wrapper.sh` is invoked from within another `pulse-wrapper.sh` context (detectable via environment variable or parent PID check), exit immediately.

3. **Lock acquisition logging**: Log when a lock is acquired vs when `_handle_existing_lock` returns 1, so the operator can see whether the guard is actually firing.

4. **Stale-lock reclaim hardening**: In `_handle_existing_lock`, add a minimum-age check: if the lock PID is alive and has been running for less than 60 minutes (`PULSE_STALE_THRESHOLD`), do NOT attempt reclaim even if `grace_period` expires. The 60-minute threshold is defined at pulse-wrapper.sh line 28 but `acquire_instance_lock` uses a different grace mechanism that can override it.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.20.86
- **Latest version**: 3.20.86
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

- #24961 — pulse REST fallback death spiral (compounded by duplicate wrapper overhead)

title: gh shim blocks headless writes for managed repo entries without explicit role
body:
## Description

A managed repository entry in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` can have `slug`, `maintainer`, `pulse: true`, and recent aidevops `version`/`updated` metadata, but no explicit `role` field. In that state, headless pulse GitHub writes can be blocked by the `gh` PATH shim as if the repo were contributor/read-only.

This blocks dispatch coordination writes such as `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments. The pulse can repeatedly see an eligible issue and pass dispatch prechecks, but the worker never launches because the claim comment cannot be posted.

## Expected Behavior

The framework should keep repo-role semantics consistent across components. Either:

1. repo registration/setup/update should backfill an explicit `role` field for initialized repos, or
2. the `gh` shim should use the same documented fallback as other role-resolution code when `role` is omitted.

For a repo with maintainer metadata indicating the authenticated user is the maintainer, unattended aidevops coordination writes should not be classified as contributor/read-only solely because `role` is absent.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
printf '{"initialized_repos":[{"slug":"example/managed-repo","maintainer":"current-user","pulse":true}]}' > "$tmp/repos.json"
AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1 AIDEVOPS_REPOS_JSON="$tmp/repos.json" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh \
  api /repos/example/managed-repo/issues/123/comments \
  -X POST -f body='test claim body' 2>&1 || true
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

**Actual output**:

```text
[aidevops][external-write-guard][BLOCK] Headless automation attempted a GitHub write to contributor/read-only repo example/managed-repo.
  This repo is observe-only for unattended pulse/routine workers. Re-run interactively or set AIDEVOPS_USER_INSTIGATED_EXTERNAL_GH_WRITE=example/managed-repo for this exact target.
```

**Expected output**:

A repo entry with maintainer metadata should not be treated as contributor/read-only merely because `role` is omitted. Either the registry should contain an explicit `role`, or the shim should auto-detect consistently.

**Causal code**:

```text
.agents/scripts/gh:275-289
- `_shim_repo_role()` reads only `.role` from repos.json.
- If `.role` is absent or not `maintainer|contributor`, it returns `contributor`.

.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md:21-26
- Documents `role` as auto-detected from slug owner vs `gh api user` when omitted.

.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh:480-518
- `register_repo()` writes/updates `maintainer`, `pulse`, `priority`, `init_scope`, etc.
- It does not write or backfill `role`.

.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:271-277
- `_post_claim()` posts claim comments through `gh api ... --method POST`.
- It redirects stderr to `/dev/null`, hiding the underlying external-write-guard reason and leaving only a generic claim failure.
```

Related closed issue found during duplicate search: #24720 (`t3598: Headless external GitHub write guard`). This report is not the same scope: #24720 added the guard; this report covers a follow-on false block when managed repo entries omit explicit `role`.

Recent relevant history observed locally:

```text
1cc6bacd6 t3598: fix headless external gh write guard (#24719)
09b168b0e fix: guard automated GitHub writes by repo permission (#24736)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a `repos.json` initialized repo entry with `slug`, `maintainer`, and `pulse: true`, but no `role`.
2. Run a headless `gh api` issue-comment POST through the aidevops `gh` shim.
3. Observe the write is blocked as contributor/read-only.
4. Add `"role": "maintainer"` to the same repo entry.
5. Observe the guard no longer blocks at the repo-role stage.

## Workarounds Applied

- Added `"role": "maintainer"` to the affected local `repos.json` entry.
- Restarted pulse after the config update.

This workaround should not be required if role auto-detection/backfill is working consistently.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.20.86
- latest version: 3.20.86
- AI assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21
- gh CLI: 2.94.0

## Additional Context

This appears to be a schema/semantics mismatch, not an OS-specific issue:

- The docs describe omitted `role` as auto-detected.
- `pulse-repo-meta.sh` has role fallback logic based on current GitHub user and slug owner.
- The `gh` shim has a stricter implementation that defaults missing role to contributor.
- Repo registration currently records `maintainer` but not `role`.
- Dispatch claim failures are hard to diagnose because the claim-post path suppresses stderr from the underlying `gh` call.

Suggested maintainer considerations:

1. Decide whether `role` should be a required persisted field or a derived field.
2. If required, add a migration/backfill for existing `repos.json` entries and ensure `aidevops repos add`, `aidevops init`, setup, and detect write it.
3. If derived, update the `gh` shim to share/replicate the same fallback semantics documented for `role`.
4. Improve `_post_claim()` diagnostics so external-write-guard failures are surfaced in pulse logs without leaking secrets or private repo names.

title: merge-stuck: pulse merge throughput collapse (5 consecutive zero-progress cycles)
body:
<!-- merge-stuck:zero-progress -->
## What

The pulse deterministic merge pass has had **5 consecutive cycles** with eligible-unmerged PRs but zero merges. The threshold is `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES=5`.

## Why

Eligible-unmerged means `APPROVED + MERGEABLE + !draft + !hold-for-review`. When this is non-zero AND the merge count is zero across multiple cycles, the merge pass is structurally blocked — gates failing closed (e.g. branch-protection 404 mis-fire), GraphQL exhaustion, repo-allowlist mismatch, or a regression in the merge gates themselves.

## How

### Files Scope

Investigation only — no `Files Scope` declared.

### Snapshot

```
eligible_unmerged_this_cycle=1, eligible_stuck_count=0, zero_progress_cycles=5
```

### Investigation steps

1. Read `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` since the meta-issue was filed (`grep 'Merge pass: skipping' `) — the per-PR skip reason is logged for every cycle.
2. Cross-check `pulse-stats.json` for circuit-breaker fires and the `pulse_merge_branchprotect_404_skips` counter — if non-zero, the t2922 fail-closed path is mis-firing.
3. Reproduce the merge gate decision for one stuck PR via `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N>` — it explains what the pulse decided and why.
4. Apply the fix (often a one-line gate adjustment) and verify the next cycle drops zero-progress to 0.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause of the throughput collapse identified.
- [ ] At least one of the stuck PRs successfully auto-merges.
- [ ] `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles` reads 0 in `pulse-stats.json`.

## Session Origin

Filed automatically by `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` (t3193). The detector resets the zero-progress counter on any successful merge — if the meta-issue is stale (cause already resolved), close it manually.

title: Fix pulse repo role maintainer metadata classification
body:
## Goal
Ensure pulse repo role resolution treats configured maintainers as maintainer-capable when the repo slug owner differs from the authenticated user.

## Context
A prior fix aligned the GitHub write guard with maintainer metadata, but the pulse role classifier still only promoted repos when the slug owner matched the current GitHub user. Org-owned repos with `maintainer` metadata could therefore remain contributor/read-only in pulse paths.

## Files
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-role-guard.sh`

## Reference pattern
- Keep explicit `role: contributor` authoritative/fail-closed.
- Promote to maintainer only when no explicit role is set and either configured `maintainer` or slug owner matches the current GitHub user.

## Verification
- `bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-role-guard.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-role-guard.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-role-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`
